name: AINews
why: Every issue has an evals cluster in its recap, often under a New evals heading. It catches launches that never become papers, such as BallotBench and Immigration Bench.

name: Don't Worry About the Vase
why: Each weekly AI roundup has an On Your Marks section about benchmarks and evals, with commentary on what they show.

name: Import AI
why: Half of recent issues lead with a named benchmark, most of them new, and explain why it matters.

name: The Epoch Brief
cadence: One or two posts a week
why: Announces Epoch's own new benchmarks and its Benchmark Reviews.

name: Interconnects
cadence: One to three posts a week
why: Mostly open models and post-training, with occasional deep reads on new evals.

name: Daily Papers
why: About one paper in five is a new benchmark. Upvotes, the author's organization and a code link come with each paper, which makes ranking easy.

name: arXiv
why: Most new benchmarks appear here first. Recall is the best of any feed, but most hits only mention benchmarks, so a filter has to do the work.

name: NeurIPS Evaluations and Datasets track
why: Every accepted paper is a dataset or an evaluation, reviewed. It arrives in one batch each autumn.

name: Benchmarking Hub
why: A curated list with independent runs and a capability index. A new row in its metadata is a benchmark worth tracking. The almanac's scores come from here.

name: Inspect Evals
why: New evals register as their own folder, so each new folder is a newly submitted, runnable benchmark.

name: Harbor Hub
why: Labs and vendors publish agent task sets here first, packaged to run. Test entries appear too, so it needs review.

name: Environments Hub
why: New eval and training environments every day. Most are for reinforcement learning, a few are benchmarks.

name: Every Eval Ever
why: A shared store of results on thousands of benchmarks. A new collection folder is a benchmark entering the corpus.

name: Official benchmark datasets
why: A curated allow-list of evaluation datasets that model cards can report against. Every entry is a real benchmark.

name: VLMEvalKit
why: New multimodal and video benchmarks land here within weeks of their papers.

name: Vals AI
why: Launches its own professional benchmarks in law, finance, medicine and tax, and announces each one on its blog.

name: SEAL leaderboards
why: Scale publishes its own new benchmarks here, each with a dated post.

name: Artificial Analysis
cadence: New evaluations several times a month
why: Its changelog announces each evaluation it adopts. Its terms bar reuse of its data in other ranking products, so the almanac links to it and imports nothing.

name: Arena
why: Adds its own arenas a few times a year. Read it through its published dataset, not the site.

name: Lab model cards and system cards
by: Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Moonshot and others
why: A benchmark that appears in a frontier lab's headline table has arrived. Open-weight labs put their tables in Hugging Face READMEs.

name: awesome-ai-leaderboard
why: The most active general list of AI leaderboards.

name: Awesome-CUA
why: Structured, dated records of computer-use agent benchmarks, kept current by a scanner.

name: Benchmark authors on X
why: Most launches that are not papers start as a thread. X's terms forbid scraping, so this one stays manual. AINews links the threads it covers.
